name: Farcaster Frames SDK
description: The official SDK for building Farcaster MiniApps (formerly Frames v2). Provides client-side APIs for accessing Farcaster context (FID, custody address, cast hash), triggering wallet transactions from within a Frame, and communicating with the embedding Farcaster client.

ecosystem_fit.notes: The only SDK for building Farcaster-native MiniApps. Every Frame/MiniApp that needs Farcaster context (FID, wallet, cast hash) uses this SDK.
Farcaster MiniApps deploy on Base. Most miniapp onchain actions execute on Base — the Frames SDK provides the wallet bridge to Base transactions.
Frames can trigger Ethereum mainnet transactions, but Base is the dominant choice for Farcaster miniapps.

common_pairings.context: Farcaster Frames SDK provides the client-side Farcaster context (FID, cast hash). Neynar provides the server-side social graph enrichment (user profile, follow graph, cast metadata). In a MiniApp, both are standard: Frames SDK for client state, Neynar for server-side social data.

Frames SDK exposes the Farcaster custody address; Privy creates or retrieves the embedded wallet linked to that identity. Use Privy's miniapp-specific configuration — the standard @privy-io/react-auth SDK has rendering issues inside Farcaster Frames.
OnchainKit provides the wallet UI components (wallet button, transaction button); Frames SDK provides the Farcaster context that lets OnchainKit know who the user is and what wallet they have.
Alchemy provides the RPC layer for reading Base chain state within a MiniApp (balances, NFTs, transaction status).

trust_evidence.description: The official Farcaster-maintained SDK for MiniApps. All production Farcaster MiniApps that access Farcaster context use this SDK.
Actively maintained by the Farcaster core team. V2 MiniApps spec represents a significant evolution from v1 Frames — the SDK reflects the current protocol standard.
Official Farcaster developer documentation covers the SDK API, MiniApp lifecycle, and wallet interaction patterns.

sdk_migration.notes: v1 Frames used @farcaster/frames-client for server-side frame handling. v2 MiniApps use @farcaster/frame-sdk for client-side context access. These are architecturally different — v1 frames are stateless OpenGraph-based; v2 MiniApps are stateful client applications. A repo using @farcaster/frames-client is building a v1 Frame and should migrate to v2 MiniApps for richer functionality. Additionally, third-party frame builder SDKs (frames.js, frog) are community alternatives to the official SDK — they use different patterns and should be detected separately.

scale_guidance.hackathon: Use @farcaster/frame-sdk directly. For rapid frame creation, frames.js or frog provide higher-level abstractions with less boilerplate.
scale_guidance.mvp: Use the official @farcaster/frame-sdk for production-quality MiniApps. Third-party abstractions (frames.js, frog) introduce additional dependency risk.
scale_guidance.production: Pin the @farcaster/frame-sdk version explicitly — the Farcaster protocol is evolving and breaking changes have occurred between minor versions. Monitor Farcaster developer Discord for SDK updates.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: Not a direct alternative — Neynar is server-side social data, Frames SDK is client-side context. Use both together in production MiniApps.

anti_patterns: Using @privy-io/react-auth (standard Privy SDK) inside a Farcaster Frame without miniapp-specific configuration — the standard SDK has rendering issues in the embedded Frame context. Use Privy's miniapp mode or the @privy-io/expo package for Frame environments.

Building v1 Frames (@farcaster/frames-client) for new projects — v2 MiniApps provide a dramatically better user experience with client-side state, wallet interactions, and full React app capabilities.

Accessing Farcaster context via Neynar only without the Frames SDK — Neynar provides server-side data enrichment, not the client-side context (FID, cast hash, wallet address) that Frames SDK exposes at runtime.
Not calling sdk.actions.ready() after the Frame renders — without this signal, the Farcaster client shows a loading state indefinitely.
Treating frames.js or frog as equivalent to the official SDK — they add useful abstractions but introduce additional abstraction layers and update lag relative to the official protocol spec.
